venarirleth.summary: Venarirleth is a fictional realm of the Arcane, shaped by resonance and oath. Its history runs from the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed out of sound at basins like Vesizis and Moraldorden, through the Age of Sundering, when the sky tore at Jorasteld and the world split into Shards bound by the Pact sworn at Ryamora. Its cities are shaped by these events: Iloramoma, a drowned glass city raised in the Fall to hold the sworn parts of the Pact, and Pelernolde, a fortified sanctuary-city of the Holy Age. Later convergences such as Ilyinnae, Craron, and Silualeth recur as tides that fold or stretch the realm's seams.

ryira.summary: Ryira is a realm of the Arcane era marked by sealed rifts, sunken cities, and luminous tides. Its places include the drowned sea of Venamuarla, the glass-island archipelago of Mienae, the fog-bound harbor of Sileinnora, and the sunken lantern-city Lyirlys. Events such as the violet-fog wave Nuarora and the Sundering of the Glasswind shaped its history, while the Silaenae siege burned its eastern cliffs in the sixth age's second year.

venaremwen.summary: Venaremwen is a fictional planet in the Arcane Realm whose history is shaped by the Seeding, when makers pressed the Weave into the ground and lulled the quiet powers to sleep. The Age of Sundering followed, marked by Anavamala, a rupture of silver fire in the sky, and Surasaari, a tide of light that split holding walls and opened crossings. Its Courts held trials and sealed doors between worlds, first with Drenurden and Kougukurn. Places include the court-city Kalukamuta, the fortress-city Graithokoth, and the hall Silaennirae, where branching futures are catalogued.

ryerlae.summary: Ryerlae is a world of the Arcane realm marked by sunken vaults, drowned archives, and shifting arcane convergences. Its places include Nuilluarys, a glass vault holding the memories of the dead, and Ilyireinae, a grove-city above a deep basin. Recurring events such as Miema, when wandering sigils bind to attuned travelers, and Veneileth, a festival of rained starlight, draw participants into its arcana. The Sundering and the Seeding of Ryerlae mark its mythic past, when worlds broke apart and the Weave was pressed into the soil.

orienna.summary: Orienna is an arcane realm whose history runs through several ages. Its first roots condensed during the Singing, when a single note drew the world's stone from the void, and the Seeding later planted the Weave across the land. Walled cities, grove-cities and glass gardens rose over the centuries, and the Courts bound doors between worlds with sworn oaths. The Age of Sundering broke the old bonds, shattering walls and drowning citadels, and the Pact was sworn over the ruins. Throughout, the Library of Outcomes has shelved the branches of Orienna's Three Futures.

ryanirae.summary: Ryanirae is a world shaped by sound and sundering. Its first roots condensed from the Singing (Coraurus, Osutanira), and its resonant stone basins, such as Moranerneld and Tarnere, still hum. The Seeding planted the Weave into the soil (Krouzhogak, Voroggar), while the Courts and Holy Age built terraced cities and bell-towers. The Age of Sundering split worlds apart (Seithiseth, Tenlamala), and the sixth-age wars brought arcane convergences such as Venilla and Lyenna. Archives such as Isastith and Ukataleno preserve the Three Futures.

ryenaerlae.summary: Ryenaerlae is a realm shaped by sound and roots. The Singing, an undated sounding, condensed the first roots of the world, and Caunus and Brestarnon both name that moment. Seronor and Venaellys are valleys still humming with the first roots, and Tiranaruta, Karnoktar and Taullum recall the Sundering and the Pact. Gokar, Fenudath, Osulanari and Thouzhurn were courts where councils judged divine trials and the first doors between worlds were argued. Oriaseonor, Khuzhak and Shisith are futures that branch and are shelved in the Library, and Craden keeps lamps burning under its shelves.

ryamiel.summary: Ryamiel is an Arcane Realm whose history runs through several eras. In the Singing, the first roots of the world condensed into the bedrock, and the Seeding saw makers plant the Weave beneath cities such as Lostaunum and Ukavasalari. The Courts of the first sovereign planned doors between worlds at places like Eliomora and Croduren, and the Walled Age produced fortress-cities such as Oseisith and Mernanum. The Age of Sundering brought landfall that cracked foundations and broke old bonds. Archive-cities like Karuthurn and Osunaoma hold branching futures, and the Holy Age keeps the sealed flame-wells and lamps alive.

silara.summary: Silara is a world layered with sacred and fallen history. Its oldest sites, like Drunestock and Xaissith, condensed during the Singing, when the world's roots first formed. The Walled Age produced fortified cities such as Ukaraloma, Ryeneima, and Gougar. The Age of Sundering split the Silaran worlds into shards, and drowned or ruined sites like Halodar, Vesasith, and Vesasith's neighbors still hum with that broken Pact. Orastes, a grove-city around a great tree, holds the shelved outcomes of the Library, and Merakanala archives branching futures as living glass.

alainiel.summary: Alainiel is an Arcane realm with many places, including the sunken necropolis Elanerla, the drifting shrine-city Orianiel, the arcane metropolis Ilyannys, and the healing sanctum Elimeinna. Its history centers on the Seeding, when makers wove the Weave and the quiet powers fell asleep, with Tarnarunath and Orontistum as key moments. Alaileth, a slender crystal seed, is one of its notable artifacts. Many other entries are unrelated modern-era media and fictional items tied to the planet only by name.

ryeralwen.summary: Ryeralwen is a world of humming roots, walled cities and drifting realms. Its first roots condensed from the Singing, and the Weave was seeded in later ages. The Walled Age brought holding walls and rival orders to harbor-cities such as Osutanala and Elamwen. Sundering-era breaches released stored ward-light and rose waters, and the Library of the Three Futures split endings into shelved branches. Its sky-harbors and archipelagos hang over cloud seas, and its archive-cities hold futures never chosen.

ryirleth.summary: Ryirleth is a realm of terraced valleys, grove-cities, and walled holds shaped by a sequence of ages. Its story begins with the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed into soil and stone. The Seeding followed, when makers sank the Weave into the land while dormant powers slept. In the Holy Age, divine councils in the Courts of Ryirleth weighed trials that shaped the doors between worlds, and sealed vaults were tested with fire. The Age of Sundering brought landfall, splitting the old bonds and breaking groves apart. The Sundering's shards were later gathered under a sworn Pact, and the realm's futures were shelved in the Library of the Realm.

elaelys.summary: Elaelys is an arcane world of drifting cities, sunken vaults, and glass sanctuaries, its skies and seas threaded with stored starlight and tidal sorcery. Miira, a garden-city of silver lanterns, is sustained by singing roots and sits above a sealed cistern of starlight. Elareirleth, a sunken vault beneath the seas, keeps leviathans bound in silver chain. Oriilora floats above the Veil of Ashen Tides, and Ilyelora is a sunken cathedral-city whose walls hold spells sung into them. Across the realm, scholars, wardens, and merchants preserve memory and magic in glass, lantern, and crystal.

silanneth.summary: Silanneth is a fractured world of many layered histories. Its Singing era produced living groves and resonant basins such as Ameolus and Ilosanala. The Seeding sank the Weave into its bedrock, with the small glass stone Peloston set into the root-lattice. The Sundering cracked the arcane lattice at Valarum, leaving drifting shards like Taurnolus and sealed citadels such as Ilyanneth. Walled cities like Anasavaloma, Tarnerdath and Osulamum held the old bonds during the Age of Sundering. The Library's drowned archives, including Veneirlae and Anasakamira, preserve branching futures.

elaennirlys.summary: Elaennirlys is a varied world of northern highlands, mountain ranges, and borderlands. Its settlements include walled towns such as Amelium, Vostarnes, and Saustium Lornium, alongside the mountain stronghold Lornus and roadside tavern-houses like Veorirnum. Dungeons are common, among them Sestum Ceontialus, Reollarnia, and Seriastia Valauror. Sacred shrines, a burial ground, a fiery volcanic region at Caunor Orinor, and island sanctuaries also appear across the land.

siliomaerae.summary: Siliomaerae is a world of arcane extremes, its realm dotted with drowned and glass-built sites. Notable places include Lyimae, a fog-bound necropolis holding a sealed warding engine; Craduldon, a walled holy city with perpetual temple flame; and Ryalleth, a vaulted emporium trading burnished alloy blades. Scholars study Eluama, a sanctuary of hanging lenses modelling existence, and Sileirae, a drowned glass cathedral whose walls resonate with hymns. Events include Ryaniel, a week-long leyline convergence, and Eleirora, a rare three-moon alignment opening a rift above the world.

siluanora.summary: Siluanora is a fictional planet of the Arcane realm, recorded across several ages. Its sixth age hosts recurring luminous festivals and convergences, including Eliolennys, Silannora, and Ryeneirwen, when lantern-stars, tide-lanterns and sealed blooms align. Its places range from drifting glass archipelagos such as Miaraennora and Nuirionora to the timber hut of Mielae at the ember marshes, the sealed vault of Lyaliorwen and the archive Elerlaereth. Earlier ages add Teres and Elirualae, groves tied to the Weave and the first sovereign.

silemuarora.summary: Silemuarora is a world whose history runs through several eras: the Singing, when its first roots condensed into resonant stone, as at Drouktuzhak, Lyarlae and Elarleth; the Seeding, when the makers sank the Weave into the soil, as at Veorum and Valanilium; the Holy Age, when the Pact was sworn and the worlds began to break, as at Ceolor and Siliriomae; the Age of Sundering, when landfall split and tides broke over Kalulamari and Serialia; and the Walled Age, when fortresses such as Taunor, Ryarae and Xaatheseth were raised. Its Library shelves the outcomes of the Three Futures, and its places still hum with old oaths.

ryelora.summary: Ryelora is a fictional planet of the Arcane realm, richly populated by sunken and drifting sites. Its entries describe a sunken academy of glass and bells called Ryerimeth, the sanctuary of Ilyama where oaths are remembered, the crystalline tuning-shard Lyaniel forged during the Singing, and the sea-cavern Nuelareth beneath frozen peaks. Other sites include the drowned harbor of Miimys, the labyrinth Venualora, the silver-veined tunnels of Mielys, and the root-city Kraktuzhoth, where the roots of the first trees hum a constant chord. Many locations hold ancient wards, lost guilds, and rival factions.

venaemeth.summary: Venaemeth is a realm of drowned archipelagos, glass-veined isles, and sealed arcane vaults. Its places include Venelae, a drowned archipelago whose reefs hum and bend compasses, and Elinnuarla, a sunken moorland with humming shrines. Lyalwen drifts as violet glass islands in the Veil, and Venillys is a submerged coral-stone reliquary. Teleorus and Fenonath are valleys where the world's roots were said to sing into stone during the Singing. Elenniel, Ameror, and the Courts of Venaemeth round out a landscape shaped by tides, glass, and old enchantment.

siluanae.summary: Siluanae is a world of varied places and materials drawn from its entries. Its landscape includes high crags with cavern hollows, highland jungles yielding a scarlet fruit dust, a drowned coastal wreck with scrapheaps, and a frozen valley hamlet of traders. Ancient tombs, sealed sanctums, and a buried palace hold guardians and monarchs. Harvestable materials range from hides and pelts to frost drops, mollusk pearls, and resonant mechanical cores, while settlements, shrines, and merchant towns offer tasks, trade, and lore.

silenioriel.summary: Silenioriel is a world of many realms, peoples, and eras, recorded only through fragmentary entries. Its histories include the fall of Mestor behind its sea wall, the revolt of scaled folk in Amenia, the burning of Renum's royal hall, and the collapse of Nires after careless sorcerers opened a gate to a fiery pit. Ancient winged serpent realms, subterranean invaders, and a sealed pocket realm used for arcane trials also appear. The surviving material is scattered and often partial, with settlements, goods, and chronicles noted alongside wars and disasters.

siliorlora.summary: Siliorlora is a world of ages and arcane places. Its history runs from the Singing, when the first roots condensed, through the Seeding of the Weave, the Holy Age of gate-sealing councils, and the Sundering that split the land into Shards. Walled Age cities such as Brurde and Isathestora rose later. The Arcane realm holds drifting glass isles, sunken groves, and resonant sanctuaries like Mieleth, Mialuannae, and Elionae, many guarded by wardens or hums of stored starlight. Its entries also include a cluster of cooking tales and food-related assays, such as a fungal blight and a bland gruel decree.

silena.summary: Silena is a realm of the Arcane omniverse whose records describe many places, events, and works. Its places include drifting archipelagos and crystal cities such as Lyirleth, Venemae, and Miimae, sunken marshes like Lyilannae, and hidden sanctuaries like Eliranneth. Recorded events include the arcane tremor Silarlenora, the tide-event Ilyameth, and the annual Ryemeiriel gathering, where citizens exchange sincere apologies. Entries also cover the Sundering, which left Amellontia's crystal terraces hanging above grey mist, and the Pact sworn in Thithess's groves. Silena's records mix arcane settings with a few entries of unrelated media.

grimukougok.summary: Grimukougok is a world of many ages. Its Martial Realm, with terraced basalt valleys, was shaped by the Singing, an undated sounding when the first roots of the world condensed out of silence, marking the start of the Holy Age. The Courts held trials of endurance at fortified sanctuaries like Vharkuggun and Halustar. In the Fall, the Sundering split the sky-anchor and shattered the world into drifting shards, sworn together by the Pact. Walled towns such as Lyimaniel, Draggurn and Thorar kept their gates through the Walled Age. The Holy Age also split its ending into three futures, recorded in the Library.

groktok.summary: Groktok is a Martial realm of war-scarred worlds, fortress-cities and forge-moons. Its places include Krugouthak, a vertical ruin-city over a dead glass sea; Veneimalwen, a walled holdfast kept by sworn orders; Drairkok, a forge-city over a buried reactor-core; and Torogun, a fortress-world guarding eastern trade lanes. Many sites are sealed, shattered or drowned, and its history includes sieges, sundering wars and the reshaping of warrior brotherhoods such as Torakoth.

ashestith.summary: Ashestith is a Martial realm of fortresses, sky-citadels, and ash-blasted worlds shaped by long wars. Its history includes sieges, orbital bombardments, dynastic collapses, and the Age of Sundering. Sites range from sunken jungle strongholds and glass-spired cities to listening outposts and sealed weapon vaults, with recurring themes of sovereignty, duelists, and resonant stone. Several places, such as Viasistanum, Sastora, and Druzhaktoth, reflect its political and cultural life.

mienys.summary: Mienys is an Arcane Realm whose history unfolds across successive ages: the Seeding and Sintostia, when makers pressed the Weave into the soil and the powers beneath the groves were lulled to sleep; the Singing, when the roots of the world first hummed into shape; and the Sundering and Fall, when landfall split the continent and the Pact of the Shards was sworn over broken worlds. Later Holy and Walled Ages saw temple orders keep sacred flame at Jorurock and Xaishasora, and walled holding-cities such as Coraullor and Ryellora guard the first crossings. Grove-cities like Tarnudonar and Venaerlalys carry the Weave's legacy, while the Library's terraces at Thudenon and Kruthaggoth hold branching futures.

orierlae.summary: Orierlae is a fictional world whose Codex entries describe many places across its realms: Leolenia, a large western island near a coastal realm; Coreornenia, a large island west of an old drowned continent; Ciarnor, a large southern island; Serenanum, a vast sea between four lands; Tausor, a cold northern isle; Cintares, a coastal realm of seafarers; Calia, a fortified eastern citadel; and Casia, a vast woodland at the western foot of a mountain range. Many entries are short, undated fragments that name lands, realms, and events without giving full detail, and several entries concern unrelated game-rule terms and card mechanics.

lyariel.summary: Lyariel is a realm of the Arcane sky, marked by floating archipelagos, crystal spires, and luminous mists. Its Holy Age centers on Oriilarae, the moment the Three Futures fork and the Library shelves each outcome in glowing halls. Temple orders in Miallirora and Ryirliel tended these branching records. The Age of Sundering left shards and sealed oaths, with the Pact of the Sundering sworn at Theizess. Settlements range from Ilyala's sovereign capital and Mierlarae's song-trading city to sanctuaries like Silioleth and Venuarina, many shaped by hum, mist, and remembered oaths.

suranareno.summary: Suranareno is a Martial-realm world whose record is dominated by serialized tales of combat and training: televised bouts, numbered broadcast chapters, and long saga cycles of fighters, rivalries, and wandering champions. Its entries include the fortified valley city of Merataleno, known for ritual duelling-halls, and the sun-scorched fortress-prison Vanasaroma. Other entries describe a sunken arena, a walled crossing-town, a market-town, and a basalt highland called Goktak, where the makers sank the roots of the Weave. The planet's chronicle also references the Night of Sworn Fire, when the first sovereign sealed the Pact.

brurnadeld.summary: Brurnadeld is a fictional world whose Codex entries span several eras, from the Walled Age to modern arena contests. Its records describe Krairnun, a walled holding with stone churches and a first stone bridge, and Ciantor, a roadside fuel depot and mending yard on the edge of a wild valley. Other places include Serallia, a green wilderness with a ruined sanctuary, and Serirnus, a high tableau of stone terraces. Much of the material concerns fighting techniques used by named combatants, including strikes, grapples, and evasive maneuvers. Many techniques are tied to particular fighters, and some are passed to successors or copied by rivals.

miimeth.summary: Miimeth is a world shaped by the Singing, a resonant note that gave its first roots form in the unformed deep. The makers later sowed the Weave into the sky during Osulannaum, lulling its quiet powers to sleep. The Sundering shattered the old worlds in Droruldon and Vorogak, scattering shards across the sky and forcing the Pact to be sworn. Its places range from walled cities such as Veolles and Miama to drowned citadels like Miillora and Silera, and floating sky-gardens such as Ryeriel. The orders of scribes, wardens, and temples keep its crossings and ancient flames alive.

alaima.summary: Alaima is a world whose entries span many regions and trials, from drowned archipelagos and crystal causeways to frozen arenas, underground vaults, and floating sky-gardens. Its places are linked by timed trials, stone dais waypoints, and guardians such as hollow armored sentinels and luminous braziers. Several locales carry hidden rewards, sealed gates, and shifting tides, while others feature hazards like chilled pools, shocking sludge, and drifting platforms. Music, tiles, and recurring tunes recur across the world, tying its scattered sites together.

torugun.summary: Torugun is a world of many places spanning several eras. Its Martial realms hold cliffside monasteries, duelling citadels and sealed arenas, while its river uplands carry walled garrison towns and holdfasts built to guard the first crossings. Ancient sites date to the Seeding, Sundering and Holy Age, when councils judged divine trials and makers wove quiet powers into stone. Ukavalari, Ukanasarala and Krugazhun mark the scars of the Fall and Sundering, and Lyemiel and Kalulauta preserve older threads of the Weave. Torugun's Sauranum ingots hum when the ground shifts.

oriamora.summary: Oriamora is an Arcane Realm world whose history runs from the Singing, when its first roots condensed and tones knotted scattered substance into land, through the Seeding, when the Weave was sown into living stone, and the Walled Age, when holding walls and holy cities were raised against drifting fog-tides and border raiders. The Age of Sundering split old bonds between drifting lands, leaving drowned cities, cracked wards and sealed galleries across the world. Its Courts once bargained over the doors between worlds, and the Library of Three Futures keeps a shelf of every outcome, with grove-cities and terraced archives where the branching futures are recorded and sometimes briefly made real.

vhoggaktak.summary: Vhoggaktak is a Martial-realm planet of fortress-cities, iron citadels and ash-scarred plains, governed by warlords, sovereigns and wardens across its ages. Its history runs from the Singing, when roots condensed into ground at Sileinuara and Syesheth, through the Seeding, when the Weave was planted at Pelardonath and Vanatamoma, to the Holy Age's Anaranoma, a night when temple-bells rang without hands and flames bent toward one shelf of the Library. Sites range from the silver grove of Nuerliriel, where the first sovereign held council, to the sunken citadel Gragak and the tiered cloud-palace Vhouzhurn. The Three Futures branch the ending at Isyustith.

crurnon.summary: Crurnon is a world of contrasts. Its sunken hollow Valausor, where the makers first planted the Weave, still hums with sleeping powers, while Breldath in the far north is a frozen tundra whose ice stores tidal energy. Brodurnath is a sprawling foundry metropolis of brass towers, and Pelurne a cinder-lit valley of gearworks and boiler-towns. Ancient court-cities such as Ilyimeth, Pelunock and Kornouggun mark the divine and martial eras, and Tentanira rose during the Singing as a terraced grove-city with bells said to ring at times of change.

ryellae.summary: Ryellae is a richly layered world of the Arcane Realm, shaped by successive ages. Its story runs from the Singing, when its first roots began to hum, through the Seeding that planted the Weave at Fenarudock, to the Fall and Sundering that split the worlds and produced the Pact. Later eras brought walled holdfasts such as Rostor and Tenrareno, and the Library of possible endings preserved in Orialeth, Thaigak and Ryilleinwen. Across its realm lie many drowned, floating and terraced places, including Venilys, Silinnora, Alaemuanna and Elinerora, each carrying its own strange lore.

khairnar.summary: Khairnar is a world whose history runs from the Singing, when its first roots condensed out of the void, through the Seeding, when makers planted the Weave and lulled the land's quiet powers to sleep. The Holy Age saw walled cities and temple orders, including Nualla and Keloldarne, keep burning lamps and judge divine trials. The Age of Sundering broke the old bonds: shelves of ground drifted apart, fortresses like Gruktogok were raised against warbands, and convergences forced the Library of the Three Futures to shelve every branching outcome at once. Ryenala and Rarnilium stand among the fractured highlands and cliffs that record this era.

eliolerae.summary: Eliolerae is a realm of the Singing and the Sundering, where drifting archipelagos such as Meranaari and Vernium hum with resonance and the sworn Pact binds the surviving orders after the Fall. Its Arcane realm holds recurring events like Elemae, a dream-song that opens once every two thousand years, and Ilyilwen, a convergence that binds mages to a single vow. Scholars also note Merasamala, a seed-lantern used by Library scribes to test sovereign decrees against the Three Futures. Beyond these, the realm contains many minor locales, from healing houses and academies to small shops and roadside stations, along with tales, songs, and broadcasts recorded across its ages.

nuimiel.summary: Nuimiel is a world whose history runs through several ages: the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed; the Holy Age, when the ending split into three futures shelved in the Library of Branches; the Walled Age, when landfall broke old bonds; and the Fall, when the Sundering shattered grove-skies and the Pact was sworn. Places include the grove-city of Silamwen, the sunken court of Krougathok, the floating archive-city Zephishora, and the reading-vault Rastanum. Events such as Seliarus, Kelodenon, Halerdulden and Jorurostath mark its turning points, and its Arcane Realm holds humming stone and branching archives.

nualireth.summary: Nualireth is a world whose roots condensed from the Singing at the undated sounding Ukasanoma, with Zepheivsis cited as a related sounding that cracked early landmasses. The Seeding, marked by Iseivsora, Khairnak, Tiarelum and Torotharnun, planted the Weave and lulled the quiet powers beneath it. The Sundering followed: Asheistith and Venilae split the worlds into Shards, and Telintanum saw the old tethers snap, after which the Pact was sworn among the surviving courts. Places include the grove-city Joruderden, the glass archipelago Anavaum, and the drowned archive-city Jorurnen, where possible endings are shelved.

torarnak.summary: Torarnak is a deep, ash-scarred world whose Martial realm is dominated by sunken fortresses, forges, and vaults carved into basalt and glass. Places such as Vhurkaithak, a black-spired citadel of sorcery, and Thaigornun, a cavern-fortress echoing with war-engines, reflect a culture of warlords, duelists, and iron-working clans. Vhagun and Drozhagurn are forge-cities, while Khougurn is a luminous hollow of mushroom-folk now troubled by rot. Ancient memories of the Seeding, Sundering, and Walled Age persist in shrines, ruins, and oath-stones across the surface and the deep.

vorairnok.summary: Vorairnok is a Martial Realm of the Codex marked by walled holds, sunken ruins, and recurring catastrophes across its eras. Walled cities such as Karnouthak, Miastilanum, and Silerys guard river crossings and fords, while sky-islands like Toragak and Thaikturn and drowned sites such as Krothurn and Druzhougoth dot its landscape. Its history includes the Sundering at Druston during the Fall, the Walled Age's rupture at Moreruldeld, and the Holy Age's trials at Kugurn and Fenunodeld. Later eras brought the Three Futures, with Nialesium, Krothok, and Sauntum recording branching outcomes shelved by the Library.

ryala.summary: Ryala is an arcane world of drifting cities, sunken sanctuaries, and luminous ruins where starlight, tides, and memory are bound into stone and glass. Lyennualeth's moss-lit grove hums with stored starlight, while Venuarlae floats as a lantern-city of bridges and relic trade. Veneilirwen rises as a drowned citadel whose gates shift with the moon's tides. Elioriel's sealed sanctum tests the minds of those who enter. Across the realm, wanderers face mirrored lakes, storm-wracked seas, and rites that can rewrite tides and oaths.

miarlinnys.summary: Miarlinnys is an arcane realm whose history runs through several ages: the Singing, when the world's roots first condensed; the Seeding, when makers planted the Weave into terraced valleys like Vesasteth, Thurne and Seorium; the Courts' trials and the building of doors between worlds at Peledar and Kelerostar; the Walled Age and its Sundering, when landfall cracked the old bonds; and the Three Futures recorded at Jorusterden. Its settlements range from harbor cities such as Mielaena to drowned chapels and sealed hollows like Elirioma, many still guarded by orders and wards.

osutaala.summary: Osutaala is a realm of many layers, shaped across successive ages. Its Ki realm holds grove-cities such as Silama, Seisora and Nuarlys, court-cities like Vesethith and Ryereilae, and walled towns such as Moradar and Drodath. Its history spans the Singing, when the first roots condensed in events like Miama and Seitheth, the Seeding of the Weave at Drouggurn and Ryillys, the Age of Sundering with its ruptures Krouggorkun and Anaramuta, and the Pact sworn at Thelde. Later eras bring the sky-citadel Osunalraala and the sealed Ukatalum, along with ruptures like Tirasanuta. The Library's branching futures are recorded in Nialium and Tarnedon.

vhaikun.summary: Vhaikun is a fictional planet recorded through a catalog of trial-ground entries, not a single world description. Its entries describe many named stages and chambers across several chapters, including sealed sanctums, fortified strongholds, and marshes. Some stages are shaped by a single maker, and several carry haunting or drifting melodies. Many include hazards such as hidden passages, spawning pits, and shifting architecture, and wanderers must pass them in sequence. Some entries describe unrelated items, such as a gas giant, a starship deck, and a medical bay, that appear in the same catalog.

lyirlora.summary: Lyirlora is an arcane realm of glass cities, drowned harbors, and luminous seas shaped by sealed convergences and ancient wars. Its places include Nualluana, a drowned archipelago of tidal glass-cities; Ilyarys, a sanctuary of silver spires over a lake of condensed starlight; and Orianniel, a sky-garden city bound by wards woven over seven eras. Its history records the Oriariel rift opened by three rival heirs claiming the Arcane Throne, the Miamora convergence that flares only moments each age, and the Venimionae cataclysm that ended the Verdant Concord. Seas, storms, and bound starlight recur across the realm.

losaustanum.summary: Losaustanum is a planet recorded through a modest set of entries, its name appearing in the entry that describes a modern district on a bright world, known for quiet streets and tight-knit residents within a larger city of the same name. Nearby in the record, Ameornum and Telentor describe distant realms reached beyond ordinary worlds, while Tarnaunia recounts a conquering people wiped out by a cosmic devourer. The surrounding entries sketch a planet of contrasts: quiet coastal and river towns, hidden strongholds, and far-off worlds of ruin and ambition. Details of Losaustanum itself remain sparse beyond its residential district.

miilora.summary: Miilora is a fictional realm whose history is recorded across many places and events. Its first age began in the Singing, when first roots condensed out of the void, and the Age of Sundering split old bonds and broke the realm into drifting fragments. Sites range from sealed vaults and drowned archives to floating archipelagos and frozen frontiers. The Library of Three Futures, where possible endings are shelved as separate records, recurs through several entries. Its sovereign and courts sealed early doors between worlds, and the realm's cosmology centers on how its world and futures took form.

nuilleimwen.summary: Nuilleimwen is a world shaped across several ages. Its first roots condensed during the Singing, when the hum of unformed light first held a lasting shape, and the first sovereign's groves and kingdoms later took root through the event Oseisora. The Seeding, in which makers planted the Weave while the Arcane Realm's powers slept, marked the Holy Age. The Courts of Nuilleimwen weighed trials for doors between worlds, until the Sundering cracked their halls. The Age of Strangers and later landfalls, including Amanoles and Elinualeth, broke the old walls and oaths. The Three Futures branch in the Library, where outcomes are shelved as they form.

tirakaluta.summary: Tirakaluta is a fictional world shaped by its Fall, the Sundering and the Pact sworn over drifting shards. Its places include the terraced grove-city Kraizhoukar, the basalt terrace Graizhar above the Sundering Deep, and the walled hold Shiasith in the Walled Age. Many events recur across the Ki realm's epochs, such as Suralauta's tide, Ukasamanuta's split sky and the seven-day seam of Surasaira. Its sealed vault-city Osumalkarum and sunken prison Merakarala show the realm's guarded and submerged sites. Several entries are serialized-tale installments and do not describe the planet itself.

oriellys.summary: Oriellys is a world shaped across several ages. In the Singing its roots first thickened into stone, and outside traders later anchored their houses to its ridges in the Age of Strangers. The Seeding brought the Weave, planted in silver-barked groves and basalt shrines by makers whose temple flames burned without fuel. In the Holy and Walled Ages, courts and councils argued over the doors between worlds, sealed them with shared oaths, and orders guarded walled cities and first crossings. The Sundering broke many lands apart, though some citadels survived. Throughout, the Library has shelved branching futures, from quiet tremors at forks in the ending to a drowned archive-city where those shelved outcomes bleed into the sea.

tianausanum.summary: Tianausanum is a Ki realm woven from many strange places: sunken cities ringing with tidal bells, drifting archipelagos of crystal and glass, frozen tree-realms, and hidden hollows where time or memory is stored. Naulia, Caurnes and Miastus hold ruins and archives, while Leostiria and Teostor preserve stillness and silence. Recurring events such as Costia, Amirnanum, Liastor and Nellirnes mark its catastrophes and rifts. Earlier ages are recorded in sites like Tirakaruta, Fenarelde and Kaizhar, where councils and first oaths shaped the world's doors between realities.

lyannae.summary: Lyannae is a realm of contrasts: glass-black ridges and sleeping furnaces in Ryeneth, drowned citadels and sunken cathedrals beneath salt marshes and lakes, and drifting archipelagos of lantern-lit harbors and bazaars. Its history runs from the undated Singing, when the first roots condensed out of drifting light, through the Age of Sundering, when landfall shattered old compacts and walled holdfasts such as Koukurn and Zephisith were tested. Arcane sites like the branching Shyuvseth hall and the Ossaline Spine's reality-thinning fog mark its magical character.

lyannora.summary: Lyannora is a world of singing stone, sundered skies, and branching futures. Its terraced valleys such as Zephezess and Vanaranoma hum with the resonance of the Singing, while Miema, a drifting shelf of glass-stone, hangs above the Ashen Sea. Walled towns like Jorerden and Tenvalira preserve the first crossings, and sundering events including Osathora, Pelardon and Sesheth mark the rupture of old bonds. Suramanala records a silent fold in the Three Futures, catalogued in the Library at Elenaereth.

oriilora.summary: Oriilora is a world of drifting archipelagos, drowned cities, and sealed realms, shaped by the Singing that first condensed its roots, the Weave planted in its soil, and the Sundering that broke old tethers. Places such as Haloduldon, Torozhak, Venaniorys, and Keledon hold archives, shelved futures, and sleeping powers. Alongside these, the record includes many short, unconnected promotional pieces: toy and merchandise advertisements, pop-up gatherings, and collaboration notices that appear and fade quickly across the planet.

torukouthar.summary: Torukouthar is a world of cliffs, valleys, and fortresses shaped by its ancient history. Its first roots condensed during the Singing, when a sounding note drew matter into stone and water (Shiathazora, Vestor). In the Seeding, makers pressed the Weave into bedrock at Vesathis and Osisteth. During the Age of Sundering, landfall broke old bonds, and rupture and council followed at Shyuthora and Fenodeld. Draiggurn, a terraced fortress-city, hosted divine trials, while Ashiaseth keeps vigil over the Sundering's seams. In the Three Futures, the Library shelves each branch of the ending.

orintanum.summary: Orintanum is not a single world in these entries but a scattered set of unrelated fictional realms, each named by a distinct id. Entries describe a ruined future world where thinking animals rule and a lone human struggles to survive, a shared web of worlds where guardians are only recently active, a sheltered refuge beyond a sea of collapsing worlds, a grim world-wide catastrophe, and a seafaring world of raiders. Many other entries cover serialized heroic chronicles, grim afterlife realms, and fictional-era stories, with no single geography or history shared among them.

thurkok.summary: Thurkok is a fictional omniverse of the Grounded realm, shaped by the Sundering, when worlds split and landfall broke old bonds. Its places range from salt basins and sunken fortresses to terraced grove-cities and walled court-cities, many marked by rusted hulks, causeways, and ruined pump-towers. Events include the Long Dimming, the Seeding that planted the Weave, the Singing that condensed the world's first roots, and the sealing of doors between worlds during the Courts. Caravan clans, toll-keepers, and scavenger brigades contest the wastes, while the first sovereign's groves and the Pact endure in scattered ruins.

ashiazis.summary: Ashiazis is a fictional planet whose entries describe a wide range of places, from terraced court-cities and grove-cities to drifting stellar fortresses and orbital foundries. Several entries recall a Holy Age, a Sundering and Fall that split suns and worlds, and a Pact sworn among the orders. Other entries describe the Library of Outcomes, which records the branching Three Futures, and the Singing that condensed the earliest roots of the world. Many locations are tied to dying stars, crystal spires, and sealed vaults.

lialintor.summary: Lialintor is a fictional world whose lore is recorded across scattered entries: tales of dread and cosmic horror, sunken provinces, and forgotten speakers tied to sleeping entities. Its Age of Sundering saw landfall break the old bonds between drifting lands, and its roots are said to condense out of the Singing. Notable places include Nelistes, a terraced hall of judges, and Kalunarum, a sunlit grove-realm where living roots bind the Weave to the soil. Many other entries are tales, pamphlets, and anthologies that circulated among readers.

amarnes.summary: Amarnes is a realm of mythic ages and sealed events. Its story runs from the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed, through the Seeding, when makers set the Weave into the soil, to the Holy Age, when temples kept fires binding the sleeping powers. The Fall brought the Sundering and the Pact sworn over the broken Shards. Walled cities such as Silenora, Grimoukun and Telilentor grew through the Walled Age, and the Age of Sundering split many of them. Its Mythic Realm holds the Library of Three Futures, where Gaiktuthar, Thashevsora and the drifting archive-city Osiasora keep every branching ending.

xaasseth.summary: Xaasseth is a stellar realm of many drifting worlds and places. Its entries describe Xaasyuzora, a dwelling carved into a dying blue giant, and Theisethora, a pale-glass archive-cradle tended by lantern-moths. Isavseth is a frozen starlight shard whose Veiled Choir tunes its shell to dying suns. Siasith is a sunless shipyard built from dead freighters, and Zephashora is a convergence where a dying sun's light forms ember-storms. Other entries include Orierwen, an archive-city torn from its moorings in the Age of Sundering, and Thaikoth, a walled stronghold of rival orders.

druderath.summary: Druderath is a fictional planet whose entries span many ages and places. Its stellar-era cities include Nernes, a glass-towered metropolis beside crumbling slums, and Serialor, a sprawling seat of government patrolled by armored automatons. Druderath's history includes the Singing, when grove-basins like Pelalde and Toresum took root; the Seeding, marked by Anaranira and the quiet hour of Eliorerlae; the Walled Age, which raised holdings such as Drukturn and Guktorkun; and the Age of Sundering, when court-cities like Thiathyss and Merasamuta opened doors between worlds. Its cosmic events include Elimys and Shistith. Many entries also describe a televised and serialized cyborg-police saga told across Druderath's cities.

zepheivseth.summary: Zepheivseth is a fictional realm of many worlds rather than a single planet, as the entries describe it as an omniverse of Stellar reaches. Its records mention a sundering known as the Fall, which split worlds into shards during the Age of the first sovereign, and the collapse of a bridge-tower in the Walled Age. Its planets vary widely: banded gas giants, frozen ice-worlds, scorched ember-worlds, and drifting stations, several shaped by ancient civilizations that vanished or left dormant engines and ruins behind.

halurdock.summary: Halurdock is a world whose history spans a Stellar realm of drifting arenas, research spires, and archive-stations, and an older surface record of groves, walls, and sundering. Its Singing-born basins and roots mark the first crust, while the Sundering split inhabited worlds into shards and the Pact was sworn over them. The Three Futures branch apart and the Library shelves each outcome. Its places include Brarneld, Kelarnore, Brolderneld, Ashishora, Elirlae, and Fenadock. Events include Suranaroma, Silemwen, Testaulles, and Halastock.

tarnordath.summary: Tarnordath is a fictional world whose entries describe two kinds of material. Several places bear its name directly: Dragoukak, a dense knot of condensing root-matter where the world's first sounding gathered; Oseizesheth, a drifting archive-city among the branches of the Three Futures whose foundations cracked during the Age of Sundering; Bradesten, the Sundering event that split the old worlds into Shards and sealed the Pact; Druzhurn, a Stellar Realm citadel-world of temples and flame that survived the Sundering; Seonia, a drifting archipelago of glassy islands; and Alailae, a basin of glass-green reeds. Many other entries are unrelated arenas, lore notes, and game-mode records and are not part of the planet's lore.

isyuthith.summary: Isyuthith is a world of the stellar realm, marked by sky-islands, sunken citadels, and drifting orbital habitats. Its history includes the Singing, the Fall, and the Sundering, when fragments scattered into the Shards and the Pact was sworn. Settlements range from floating harbors and glass amphitheaters to terraformed worlds and salvage hubs around dying suns. Rupture events such as Kroktuthun and Syustith reshaped its orbits. The Library of Branches shelves the futures that split at moments like Fenurdeld and Tarnarden.

drerdunen.summary: Drerdunen is a world of varied sites and materials. Mellauror is a golden-blossom meadow north of a glowing stone ring, and Oristus is a rural grove of puzzle-shaped trees. Tiastarnus holds a sealed relic beneath a great tree, and Telostum tracks rising danger as enemy troops close in. Common crafting materials include Valenia Niastinum, a heat-resistance component, and Mausintum, used in viral-protection enhancements. Ceoles is a shadowed mineral deposit site, and Sauleonus is a fortified island hideout of raiders.

pelanode.summary: Pelanode is a stellar realm of wildly varied places: Halelde, a drifting frozen world-orchard with sweet haze and churning lakes; Haluldodath, a vast observatory-fortress harvesting a dying red giant's light; Elanwen, a living grove of silver-barked trees; Jorurenock, a volcanic basin of molten rivers; and Thustenock, a sealed vault whose lever governs every living engine in the system. Events include Crurnaldath, a dying star's resonant collapse, and Pelarnoston, a radiant convergence that seeded dormant worlds. Wars such as Fenuroldeld scorched dominant city-states across millions of cycles.

linaustia.summary: Linaustia is a mythic world of sunken cities, sky-citadels, and drowned archipelagos. Its places include Telaurontia, the sky-city where the Linaustian pantheon convenes; Valeoles, a sun-drenched archipelago of terraced valleys; and Liantor, a drifting reef-island storing storm-kings' seeds. Sunken vaults such as Lasiarnia, Niriallum, and Rirnanium hold broken gods, sacred fire, and oath-glass. Riasauntor, the Sundering of Veyrath, a ten-year conflict between the Aurant Dynasty and the Thessaly Moots, marks a turning point. Osulanraari opens the Age of Sundering when the Weave is sown.

maurantium.summary: Maurantium is a fictional realm of varied places and seasonal cosmetics. Notable locales include Karouthokun, a terraced sanctuary where the orders of the Holy Age once gathered, Caseles, a walled market town beneath a fortress, and Saustia, a high-tech military stronghold on a snowy cliff. Tiantalles is a sunlit coastal hamlet, and Meosia a desert resort by a still lake. Many entries describe collectible gestures, tunes, emblems, and trinkets earned through seasonal reward tracks or bought from merchant stalls. Siallus, a tidal convergence, erupted during a fourteen-day festival of solar bloom when three moons aligned.

thivsora.summary: Thivsora is a fictional planet whose entries span the Singing, Walled Age, Courts, Sundering, Seeding, Fall and Three Futures across its many named places. Its record includes the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed, and Elarla, a flare of light that tore open cloud over three provinces during the Walled Age. Fenune marks the Sundering that split worlds from their suns and led to the Pact. Locations include Karugokun, a humming basin and neutral anchorage; Drarnulde, a hall of divine trials; Torogoth, a grove-kingdom holding the Weave's roots; Venaeniel, a temple-city keeping the Three Futures; and Fenernudar, a walled city guarding river crossings.

lernaunus.summary: Lernaunus is a richly layered world of courts, groves, and shattered realms. Its history spans the Singing, when roots broke the surface, and the Seeding, when makers pressed the Weave into the soil while quiet powers slept. The Sundering split old bonds and cracked worlds apart, after which the Holy Age's Pact was sworn over drowned islets. Divine trials at Ilolaruta and Shiaseth decided the first doors between worlds. Its sky-realm of Telianentus, its underworld of Lastor and Riasum, and its grove-cities such as Conirium and Ameolia all keep echoes of these ages.

shizasha.summary: Shizasha is a fictional planetary setting whose entries span several kinds of places. Vesezishith is a drifting mineral archipelago orbiting a dying red giant, home to Thessarine pilgrims who carve memories into stone. Xaiseshith is a plasma lattice at the spiral's fringe, with a fusion crucible feeding orbital habitats. Shiastith is a shattered stellar relay-world with a crystalline ocean. Isizasha is a crystal-garden sanctuary tended by quiet makers, and Ryamae is a grove-kingdom of terraced orchards. Many other entries cover arenas, ruins, outposts, and salvage yards, along with a ranked tournament circuit and several contested battlegrounds.

shiavsora.summary: Shiavsora is a stellar system whose worlds and structures recur across many eras. Its planets and stations include Thiazis, a sealed research outpost around a violet gas giant, and Osestora, an orbital depot famed for crystal ore trade. Other sites include Zephazith, a pocket of nonlinear time inhabited by the Veilkin, and Vesazis, a sealed archive-world. Recorded events include the Hollowing of the Twin Suns, a fleet broken in a single afternoon, and Shathis, a resonance cascade silenced by a harmonic broadcast. Its history features rival powers, treaties, and lost civilizations.

zepheistith.summary: Zepheistith is the stellar realm within which the planet's entries are set. Its places include Syisheth, a reef of crystallized starlight drifting between dying suns; Shethis, a colossal city-ship adrift in the void and home to the Shethiri; Osyustith, a fortress-palace overlooking a silver estuary; Zephyuthyss, a floating crystal spire above glacial plateaus; and Thastora, a drowned world of glassy tidal shoals. Other entries describe Sisheth, a seventeen-hour stellar convergence occurring once every six ages, and Sazeseth, a floating archipelago of crystalline spires orbiting a dying red dwarf.

syuzeth.summary: Syuzeth is the planetary designation under which this set of Codex entries is catalogued. The entries describe a range of worlds in its stellar realm: Eleinnila, a grove-city where the Courts convene and the first threshold-doors were built, and Saullum, a walled holy city tested during the Age of Sundering. Other places named include Vesastora, a frozen world of gateways, and Zephasteth, a swamp hollow with a silver moon. Many entries record worlds grouped in distant sectors, with planet counts given but no further detail.

oseivsizith.summary: Oseivsizith is the name given to a set of fictional entries that mainly cover its stellar-scale places and events. Its drifting orbital installations include Vesyuthora, a warden-station guarding the archipelago's outer lanes where cadets train, and Sheisora, a dockyard that once serviced the Veshan Concord's fleet. Xaisasha is a necropolis of dormant hulls orbiting a red dwarf. The world's history includes the war of Iseithazora, fought as the suns dimmed, and the phenomenon of Syutheth, a resonance cascade from a dying binary pair. Its surviving records date events against a single turning point.

crare.summary: Crare is a world of many fortified and grounded places tied to its ages. Its grounded realm holds sealed relay complexes like Halorde, ridge-forts such as Brestulde, and launch sites like Moranoldar that build lifters for Freedom-class craft. The Crare of the Singing and the Courts recalls grove-cities such as Orianae and Naresor, council halls like Elimys and Crarnunath, and the first roots condensed in Xaashis. The Seeding and Sundering appear in Alaemora and Nuerualora, while fens, plateaus, and drowned towns like Theste and Kelareldock shape its landscape.

kroukagar.summary: Kroukagar is a fictional world whose recorded entries span a wide range of places and objects. Its sites include a rail halt in a poisoned valley, a telescoping mountain passage linking a scorched waste to a marshy lowland, a sunken marsh lair, and a sealed testing chamber. Its objects include a tipped-over hauling vehicle, a paper note left as a clue, and a recorded message-disc kept by a woman named Ondrae for her daughter. Settlements range from a flooded city and a walled desert prison to a bogland roadside eatery and a fortified harbour. Taken together, the entries depict a land of ruins, frontier outposts, and remembered histories.

corialor.summary: Corialor is a world of many layers, shaped by a sequence of ages. Its earliest history is the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed in hollow valleys like Thiavsora and Vanavameno, and the Seeding followed, when the Weave was planted across the sky and sleeping powers were lulled, as at Elinaemwen and Lasanum. The Holy Age brought flame, temples and sworn orders, including Elualannae and Vanalanum. The Fall and Sundering broke the old bonds, sundered the worlds into Shards, and left Isiashora and Keludock as monuments of that rupture. Corialor's places range from courts and archives to drowned cities, sky-islands and realms of the dead.

veneiluana.summary: Veneiluana is an Arcane Realm whose history spans the Singing, when the first roots condensed out of resonant silence, through the Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds and split the sky into drifting Shards. The Pact was sworn over the broken worlds, and the Courts later debated the doors between worlds in terraced councils. The Walled Age brought fortified holds and tolling bells against rising flame. Places include glass archipelagos, sunken cities, reading-halls holding the Three Futures, and drowned cathedrals beneath abyssal seas, many still humming with the stored strain of ancient events.

veneruamora.summary: Veneruamora is a fictional world threaded through many fragments: a sunken lattice of crystalline groves called Venanioreth, guarded by the sentinel Orsamir, whose sap-rivers hum with stored arcane current. Its records include a hand-drawn chart covering distant northern ice, a dark-metal word-root, and a pale metal prized by a valley people. Succession and dynastic changes recur, alongside chronicles of dark raiders, a river city razed, and a great clash ending a long war. Its lore also carries shrines, sunken and walled cities, and an island kingdom raised from the ocean.

corolor.summary: Corolor is a mythic realm of contrasts: drowned tidal cities such as Valanauntus and Oresium, the grove-kingdom of Thaldon bound by an old Pact, and the windswept highlands of Vintus. Its far reaches hold a sunlit coast at Serones, a frost-bound grove at Amenia, and the scholarly archive-district of Naurnium. Political life includes a sky-city throne at Amornianes, fortified border watchposts guarding mountain gaps, and a long-ago uprising that overturned a ruling caste of makers. Its geography is marked by deep marshes, a central land split by high crags, and a scatter of sea-isles.

caustiantes.summary: Caustiantes is a richly layered world of drowned cities, sacred groves, and frozen wastes, shaped by the Seeding, the Sundering, and the Age of the Walled Cities. The Seeding sank the Weave into the bedrock and sent its powers to sleep at sites such as Miemuannora, Vhuthun, and Kelorduren. The Sundering split old bonds through landfall and sea-breaking, drowning places like Moraroneld and Pelunen. Later ages brought renewal in Oraullisus, rites like Coralia and Draizhun, and cataclysms such as Tiallonus, a three-year frost. Its realm holds fortresses, courts, and sanctuaries, with powers and wardens guarding every threshold.

kelordaren.summary: Kelordaren is a world shaped by the Singing, the Seeding, the Sundering and the Holy Age. Its valleys, such as Ilokaramari and Tentamraala, hold the earliest roots of the land, while Torazhugun and Zephivsis record the Weave's planting and the early growing kingdom. Events like Thevsora, Meosium, Draikuzhar and Sallium mark its turning points, from the first condensing of roots to the sealing that pulled the broken shards back into one sky. Walled towns such as Vaurum, Meratauta and Karnok, and the market-towns of Kouzhaithok and Xaisora, show a world where thresholds, trade and futures are contested and recorded.

venilleth.summary: Venilleth is a world whose history runs through several ages: the Singing, when its first roots condensed, the Holy Age and the Courts where divine trials and council-halls were built, the Fall and Age of Sundering that split sky and severed old bindings, and the Three Futures overseen by the Library. Its places include hollow valleys that still hum with the first chord, terraced grove-cities that hold the Weave and the Pact, floating archipelagos of stormglass and salt-white stone, drowned cathedral-cities and reading-halls where branching outcomes are shelved, and a walled stronghold of the Walled Age. The Sundering-tide Braruldath and the event Noriantes mark the world's great breaks, and the Three Futures event Amarelanum marks the fracture of its ending into branches.

corentium.summary: Corentium is a world shaped by a sequence of ages. In the Singing, the first roots of the world condensed into standing stone, marked by the sounding Siliomwen, and places like Tarnesten and Pelerdar took shape. The Seeding, recalled in events like Anakaleno, Craron and Coraloria, pressed the Weave into soil and sky and lulled the quiet powers to sleep, with temple terraces at Tirataeno and Kaikun burning sacred fire. The Sundering split worlds into Shards during the Fall, bound by the Pact, with sites such as Syestora, Naunolus and Vhoukurn. Walled holdings like Vesiazith and Broreld later guarded the crossings, while the Courts sealed doors between worlds. Branching futures unfold in the Library's grove-realms at Halenar and Osasteth.

thonurde.summary: Thonurde is a fictional planet of many grounded places across six ages. Its sixth-age world includes sunken grottos like Creldonen, reed-fen cities such as Kelurnesten, and the fortified harbor of Kelernonath. Storehouses and research sites appear too: Cradorne, a sealed vault holding surviving grain strains, and Therneld, a marsh compound of the Verdant Concord. Earlier ages add Thyuzis, a hall of divine trials, and Shevsora, a grove-valley that swore the Pact after the Sundering.

jorernodath.summary: Jorernodath is a fictional world whose history runs from the Singing, when its first roots condensed out of the still deep, through the Holy Age and the Seeding, into the Walled Age of river-towns and holding walls. During the Age of Sundering, landfall and a sky-rupture broke old oaths and reshaped its councils and crossings. Its places include the grove-kingdom of Naures, the walled market town of Meravanari, and the court-town of Crernadock, where the Council of Doors met. Entries here are fragmentary, so the account of the world remains partial.

thonudeld.summary: Thonudeld is a grounded realm of varied places and events, from fen-country Peloron and the reef-city Morunedeld to the sun-bleached estate of Tarnunath and the mannequin town Halordeld. Its settings include salt-marsh Morunar, tidal Brodeldock, and floating power platform Kelureld. Its history carries echoes of the Sundering and the Pact, seen in Suranamum and Ryela, and of later covert operations such as Tarnudock, Thunelde, Branedar, and the failed Craldornen uprising. Many assay entries (arenas, music pieces, and achievements) are also tied to the planet.

tarnaldath.summary: Tarnaldath is a stellar-scale realm of the sixth age, where a dying sun's light and drifting worlds shape its many places. Haluranen, Kelostelden, Crostudon and Droldeste are among its named worlds, each with its own luminous lattices, crystal spires, or glass cities. Its tidal and stellar phenomena include Thastar, a flare marking the sixth age, and Fenane, a convergence recurring every sixth era. Surviving peoples tend lanterns, bells, and mirrors while they wait out the cosmos's slow collapse.

kelolden.summary: Kelolden is a world of contrasts, rich in both wild growths and crafted industry. Its natural landscape includes red-to-violet palms, hard fungi, and stone spires, while its resources span coal-black ore, dark crystalline fuel, corrosive fluids, and frosted separation facilities. Its civilization is documented through grove-cities such as Vanamalum and the terraced stone-temple city of Xaastith, and through the Library's records of the Three Futures, including the events Kelurne, Tenvaroma, and Rastum. Industrial works convert ore and crude into fuels, bars, and research tokens used to advance technology.

bronurneld.summary: Bronurneld is a richly layered planet spanning many eras, from the Singing that first bound soil to sky, through the Seeding when the makers planted the Weave to lull the quiet powers, to the Holy Age of temple cities like Vesizeth and Ukasaum. Its Courts of Tirasaum and Ilonalum hold divine trials, while the Grounded realm offers river towns, salt-chapels, and ruined industrial metropolises such as Brore. Later eras bring survival tales of infected hordes, collapsed rail yards, and refuges that wanderers must fight through to reach rescue.

oriarium.summary: Oriarium is a mythic cosmos whose record spans primordial forces, sovereign gods, and sunken realms. Its origins involve a self-kindled spark that split into nine powers (Meontalor) and a sounding that condensed the world's roots (Valeosum). Later eras bring the Sundering that broke the old worlds (Ilonarum), the sky-sundering that withdrew the celestial sovereign (Miantum), and the Holy Age trials of the Courts. Sites range from the drifting island Nintum to the sunken archive-city Orestor, the walled Vanakalira, and the underworld vault of Noles, linked by recurring waters, flame, and drowned bells.

tarnornath.summary: Tarnornath is the subject of the Codex entries listed here, though the entries describe a wide range of distinct places, peoples, and objects rather than a single coherent planetary profile. Fenerde is the one entry explicitly identified as a grounded world of Tarnornath: a place of cold basalt plains and wind-carved spires where old tide-cities sank into mist. Other entries describe hidden sectors, ancient smithies, relay networks, and shelters tied to the wider setting. The record therefore presents Tarnornath as a varied, layered region shaped by long-vanished peoples and surviving remnants.

serarnum.summary: Serarnum is a fictional world whose history runs through several ages. Its first roots condensed during the Singing, a sounding recorded in the first age. In the Seeding, the makers sank the Weave into its soil and the quiet powers fell asleep beneath the groves. The Age of Sundering split the old bonds between worlds, and the Pact was sworn over the shards so the survivors could name the new order. Holy cities such as Mantianium and Craldestock grew around temples of flame, while the Library of the Three Futures shelves the branching endings of the world.

karugurn.summary: Karugurn is a fictional planet of sunken cities, drowned valleys, and fortified garrisons, shaped by the Singing, the Seeding, and the Sundering. Its places include Karouktoth, a moss-bound terrace-city whose people left carved lintels and wind-chimes behind; Vornestus, a drowned valley with towers above a grey lake; and Garkoukar, a basalt fortress that has guarded a ford for seven ages. Its ruins and shrines hum with slow resonance, and several sites, such as Khaggak's sealed hollow and Graiktuthun's warped sky, carry dangers. Local materials like Seorium and Ameontanum were traded or used for warmth in earlier ages.

silia.summary: Silia is a fictional planet whose history unfolds across the Singing, the Seeding, the Holy Age, the Walled Age, and the Three Futures. Its places range from marsh-cities and drowned sanctuaries to grove-cities humming with first root-sound, walled holy cities kept by flame-orders, and basalt citadels that shelve every branching future. Key events include the Singing, the Seeding that plants the Weave and lulls quiet powers to sleep, the Courts where divine judges sealed the first doors between worlds, and the Pact sworn over the burning of Veyrath's hall. Temple orders of flame recur throughout, guarding sleepers, tending perpetual fires, and holding back tides and armies.

seornum.summary: Seornum is a grounded world of terraced groves, walled river-ports and cliff temples, shaped by a sequence of ages. Its origins are marked by sounding events in which roots condensed from the dark and the land settled into place. The Courts of the second age held divine trials that sealed passages between worlds, while the makers of the Holy Age planted the Weave and kept temple fires burning. The Fall and the Age of Sundering split roads, bridges and oaths, and the Pact of the Shards was sworn among the scattered holdings. Settlements such as Sistora, Orallostor and Ristaurnum endured through the Walled Age, and Drasterneld and Ukatamlaira copied the Library's shelved futures.

telones.summary: Telones is a mythic world of many faces: sunlit citadels like Leostor, drifting archive-cities like Shethora, singing reefs like Cantanum, and glass cathedrals like Telosum. Its skies are marked by recurring convergences such as Vosor, Lesiastium and Mesanum, whose effects range from drowning tides to the quiet unweaving of omens. Its places hold memory, debt, and oath, from Amaustum's buried ancestral seeds to Celliror's sealed contracts. Across its ages the Singing, the Age of Sundering and the Weave shaped its roots, its orchards, and the fate of its realms.

vesiathith.summary: Vesiathith is a star system and planetary cluster in the Codex, home to a wide range of worlds: drowned glass-spired oceans, frozen moons, gilded merchant worlds, and foundry worlds. Its history is marked by many events and wars, including the Sundering of the Vaelith Concord, the Dawn Ember, and the Sundering Hymn. Its settlements range from the domed capital Seivseth to the Thessk-Ilan cities of Vesezora. The entries describe a long record of betrayal, rebellion, and trade across the system.

zephessith.summary: Zephessith is a fictional planet whose sky and orbit are crowded with places across several ages. In the Seeding, the makers planted the Weave and the Holy Age began. In the Walled Age, holding walls and orders stood firm, and in the Age of Sundering, landfall broke old bonds. The record includes the terraced valley of Miemys, the walled hill-city of Santeornus, the sundered Gathairkar, and many drifting stations in the sixth age, such as the trade hub Xaaseth and the fortress Osiathezith. In the seventh age, the archives of Silaenniel and Guthak hold the outcomes of branching futures.

elamirla.summary: Elamirla is a world of walled holds, grove-cities, and courts, shaped by the Walled Age, Holy Age, and Age of Sundering. Its places include Anamalum, a drifting cloister-shoal of glass walls; Veneimae, a basalt valley whose stone still hums from the Singing; and Tentus, a sunken terrace-city where scholars read possible futures from the Library's shelves. Walled cities such as Crudaldath and Isethith held through the Sundering, while the Courts of Elamirla bound doors between worlds at events like Gournar and Kalutanari. Across the planet, living groves, humming stone, and first crossings recur as signs of the world's oldest roots.

vesizathith.summary: Vesizathith is a fictional stellar realm of drifting orbital habitats, dying suns, and recorded catastrophes. Its places include Osistith, a hollow-star lighthouse, and Isiazeth, a vast habitat ringed by a thick shell, while Asheistora is a drowned metropolis of glass spires. Its events include Syithaseth, the collapse that ended the Varnish Accord, and Vesiatheth, a convergence of disciplined forges channeling a dying star's fire. Surviving records and sealed archives preserve the realm's history across several eras.

theivsis.summary: Theivsis is a fictional stellar realm whose records, drawn from its entries, describe a cosmos of dying red giants, drifting orbital cities, and crystalline spires. Places such as Thazess, Veseishora and Thizeth are described as seven-age-old lattices and sealed archives. Events include the Thornmarch Accord, marked by orbital molten rain, and Osiseth, which rewrote timelines across worlds. The Singing, Age of Sundering and Seeding frame its early history, while the Vesper Concord and Veshari plains appear among its political and geographic records.

fenarnock.summary: Fenarnock is a Grounded Realm world whose history runs through the Singing, the Seeding that planted the Weave, the Holy Age of temple orders and divine trials, the Sundering that split its landmass into shards, and the Fall that sank the land and sealed the Pact. Its settlements include terraced court-cities such as Torarnoth and Corenaurium, walled market towns such as Pelureldath and Grothurn, and the drowned tide-town of Sereollus. Recorded events include Halurdar, a judicial event of divine trials, and Fenurock, the sundering that sworn the Pact among survivors.

shyuthora.summary: Shyuthora is a setting of many stellar-scale events and places. Thiashora is a convergence where two dying suns braid their light into one lattice, heralding rare resonance. Ashazora is a flare-cascade erupting from a dying red giant's corona every few thousand years. Theizessora is a dimming ritual across a young star cluster ending in silent collapse. Vesiazeth is a collapsing cascade in a dying binary's heart. Syushith is a rogue convergence of dying suns burning for two ages, reshaping nearby orbits. Osestora is a frozen basin where wardens keep the land starved on purpose. Xaaseth is a tidally locked desert world concealing sealed archives.

venualys.summary: Venualys is a realm of frost, glass, and arcane current. Its landscape holds frozen seas, glacial spires, and humming crystal hollows such as Siliomeina and Veneinys. Ancient history runs through it: the Singing that first gathered the world's roots, the Seeding that planted the Weave, the walled ages of sealing and defense, and the Sundering that cracked the worlds apart. Settlements range from lattice-cities and walled fortresses to frost-bitten hamlets and archive-cities that drift above the Three Futures. Sealed vaults beneath glaciers hold dormant powers, and the realm's peoples trade, pray, and guard their wards against these forces.

kaktun.summary: Kaktun is a fractured world whose history runs through several ages. In the Age of Trials and Sundering, walled Courts such as Khothurn, Ilyannuara, Sallor and Vorouthurn judged divine trials and laid the first footings between worlds. The Seeding saw makers plant the Weave in valleys like Syazasha, Elaemiel and Gaiktak. Later eras brought the Walled Age, with holdings like Karuktoth and Tarnaldorne, and the Fall, marked by Kharnoth, a blight that shattered the old order. Today the land is scattered with ruins and survivor settlements such as Vorouthar and Grimaithok.

sestia.summary: Sestia is a mythic world of sea and sky, rich in drowned realms, floating isles, and volcanic mountains. Its afterworlds include the drowned necropolis of Liarnium, the tide-warden's Maulanum, and the sunset afterworld of Liantium. Its history spans the Singing, the Seeding that planted the Weave, the Sundering that split lands into shards, and the Walled Age, when cities like Vorukaiktun and Anakarmanum rose. Sestia's myths tell of sovereigns, elemental quarrels between fire and rain, and the sealing of the sky-dawn divide.

reoria.summary: Reoria is a mythic world of many realms and eras. Its places include the cloud-garden Telernalor above the Ashvein Sea, the drowned terrace-city Corasus, the sunken forum Serirum, and the lightless vault Melum beneath its roots. Events range from the Singing that condensed the world's first roots (Lyina, Kalutaum) to the great turning Vastes that set the sun and moon in the sky. Courts and hall-cities such as Vesisteth judged divine trials, while sieges and wars like Amenolium and Orialirium shaped its histories.

ninteostor.summary: Ninteostor is a mythic world of many realms, a planet whose entries range from sunken cathedrals and drifting citadels to glass-spired pilgrimage halls and sealed manors. Its records speak of the Singing, the Age of Sundering, and the Pact of the Shards, when broken worlds and sworn oaths shaped its lands. Many of its realms, like Ameoralles, Mernus, and Rinaurnia, are described as shadowed or drifting thresholds tied to restless spirits and forgotten bargains.

halardore.summary: Halardore is a world shaped by hums and oaths. Its first roots condensed in soundings such as Kelerude, Xaestithora and Vorourkoth, which the first sovereign's groves answered. The makers planted the Weave at Tenransaum, and the Pact was sworn over broken shards at Drureld. The Sundering later tore walled towns like Conus, Drasten and Syushiazith apart. Terraced cities including Vaullernes, Sallum and Mienwen still keep their lamps, orders and river crossings, while Xaezess holds the scars of the breaking.

thurdock.summary: Thurdock is a world of grounded realms shaped by successive ages. Its story begins in the Singing, when the first roots condensed into soil and stone, with places like Mesium and Khurkurn still humming with that tone. The Seeding brought the makers, who planted the Weave across the fields, as at Osyuthis and Tarnardock. The Walled Age followed, with holding walls and guild orders, and then the Sundering and Shards tore old bonds apart; the Pact was sworn among survivors at places like Karouggar. The Holy Age saw temple orders keep sacred flames burning in towns such as Kalulanum and Brunar.

seresum.summary: Seresum is a fictional world of sprawling canopies, cold caverns, and blighted gorges. Its wilds yield pelts, shimmering ores, and glowing crystals, while travelers find ruins, luminous shrines, and hollow mahogany titans. Its realms vary from shadowed underground halls to frozen lands and sky-spire fragments, and its gathered materials are shaped into furniture, tools, and armor. Hidden seeds and village moods further alter how the world unfolds.

seraurnanum.summary: Seraurnanum is a realm of many places shaped by successive ages. Courts once met in terraced cities such as Orialla, Khagouzhurn, Thiazasha and Crorden, where trials and the first doors between worlds were decided. The Seeding, marked by Toroggazhun and Oriinuameth, pressed the Weave into stone to sleep. The Sundering and the Fall of Seraurnanum split the world into Shards, and the Pact at Branere followed. Later eras brought walled cities like Selantum, the archive-city Syestith, and Mintus, a fortified city-state of trained citizens.

menteores.summary: Menteores is a realm of resonant stone, shattered sky-archipelagos, and sealed gates between worlds. Its story begins with the Singing, when the first roots condensed out of sustained tones, as recorded at Vosastor and Ilotamum. The Sundering and Fall later split the old worlds into Shards, and the Pact was sworn over the wreckage. Walled cities such as Gaiktok, Brestath and Corentor kept holding watch in later ages, while the Library at Miallontor shelved the Three Futures of its endings.

syezeth.summary: Syezeth is a world born in the Singing, when its first roots condensed from the void during the Holy Age. Its entries center on sites and objects tied to that origin: Meravaroma, the Singing itself, and Sathora, the bright tone that drew matter into lattices. Kaiggaktar, a basin where the first roots condensed, was ringed with flame-temples whose orders tended the sounding. Seishazeth, a resonant seed-lattice grown in the Singing, bent early groves toward a single sovereign. Shiastora and Tillium, terraced grove-cities, reflect the sovereign's gardens and the orchards where early kingdoms sprouted.

morarneld.summary: Morarneld is a realm of basalt shelves, terraced grove-cities and walled court-towns, shaped by the Singing that condensed the first roots, the Age of Sundering that split old bonds and raised doors between worlds, and the Holy Age of orders and temples. Keledorock hums with wind through its fissures, Vesizith's roots form a living lattice, and Tarnolde and Kelerath held councils beneath stone gates. Events such as Ilonaruta, Vanatamira and Thyuthis mark the undated sounding of the Singing, while Xaezora pressed the Weave into the soil. Records also catalogue many honours, trials and grim achievements.

vesizora.summary: Vesizora is a fictional world whose history is recorded across several eras. Its Singing gave rise to resonant root-lattices at Voroktar, Halenurdeld and Fenornar, and to the cavern-world Oseisithora. In the Seeding the makers left sleeping lattices such as Kelonurar and Droktak, and during the Age of Sundering Xaivsesora, Riasia and Isethora played central roles. Later eras bring the Stellar realm: Shiasezeth, Ashiavsith, Xaesora, and the dead system of Osevsith, along with wars and catastrophes like Sesora, Vesyuvsith and Shiashora. The Library's Three Futures are kept at Alaareth, Surasanira and Thiseth.

tasianium.summary: Tasianium is the planet whose entries describe a world of many distinct realms and peoples. Its lands include Caurniarium, a vast northern continent bounded by an icy ocean to the north and three great waters on its other sides, and Narium, a vast body of salt water stretching across the world that shares its name with its ruler. The planet also holds Cantus, a sunken cathedral-city built on the bones of an older empire, and Valernilium, a fog-bound harbor city beneath a vault of silver bells. Its sacred and spiritual places include Seostorum, a guarded sea-island seat, and Naureosanum, a sunken sanctuary beneath the sea. Dark and troubled currents recur, including the sickened resonance of Telestor and the restless dead of Amornerus. Recorded events and prophecies run through the entries, such as the quiet hour of Mierora in the Seeding.

venileth.summary: Venileth is a world of sunken cities, walled holdings and sealed archives, shaped by successive ages. The Singing condensed its first roots, and the makers later sank the Weave into the bedrock during the Seeding. The Pact was sworn across broken worlds in the Sundering, leaving drowned cathedral-cities and glowing lagoons behind. The Holy Age brought flame-temple orders, while the Library's shelves hold the Three Futures, where the ending forks into branching paths. Walled towns and their keepers guarded the crossings throughout.

tarnor.summary: Tarnor is a world whose history is layered across several ages. Its valleys and stones still carry traces of the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed, and of the Seeding, when the makers pressed the Weave into the soil and the quiet powers fell into their long sleep. The Age of Sundering brought landfall and the divine councils of the Courts, whose terraced cities such as Lyilae and Nases still hum with old oaths. The Fall split the sky, scattering shards that the Pact was sworn to bind. In the Three Futures, the Library of Tarnor copies branching outcomes onto brass shelves, while drowned places like Halestune and Telineranum hold the memory of lost peoples.

graikurn.summary: Graikurn is a world of many ages and settings, from the grove-cities and basalt courts of the Holy Age and the Sundering to the grim, rust-stained grounded districts of the sixth age. Its places range from terraced valleys and sealed cisterns to sunless metropolises and sprawling underground warrens. Its events include the Singing that condensed the world's roots, the Sundering and Fall that scattered the Shards, the drowning of the eastern cities, and recurring ritual and seasonal occurrences such as Kraithaggak, Kougokurn, and Karkuggar, the siren-bell that announces war.

coriarnes.summary: Coriarnes is a mythic, largely drowned realm of tidal cities, sunken cathedrals, and glass archipelagos, where the Three Futures fold and sing through standing stone and black glass. Its history runs from the Singing that rooted the world, through the Seeding that planted the Weave, to the Age of Sundering. Scattered across the land are hidden shelters where travelers rest and craft, alongside clues in notes and letters, and grim sicknesses such as the bloodsucker-haunted streets and a blood-curse threatening a crowded city. Its fortresses, cisterns, and bazaars hold tides, memories, and vows.

breroldock.summary: Breroldock is a grounded-realm planet of many places and events across its ages. Its landscapes range from basalt valleys humming with residue of the Singing, such as Osuralmaari and Siseth, to sunken vault-cities like Keluronath and flooded settlements like Pelaston.
